title: System Multiplexer Failed Event
description: A terminal multiplexer session (zellij) hosting operator agent panes lost its server without the operator asking: it panicked, was OOM-killed, or was found absent when the watchdog started (reboot, power loss, livelock reboot). Every agent pane in it died mid-task. Emitted by zellij-sentinel (infra/scripts/zellij-sentinel), which then sends the bloodbank.system.multiplexer.resume command (causationid = this event's id, same correlationid) once the session is back. Root fact: causationid null, a fresh correlationid per incident. See bloodbank/docs/event-naming.md (system, multiplexer).

ordering_key.description: §11.1 bucket multiplexer:<multiplexer>:<session>, shared with the resume command and the resumed outcome. bin/bb-emit derives it from data.multiplexer and data.session.

multiplexer.description: The multiplexer whose server failed. A new multiplexer is a new enum value in a schema revision.

server_pid.description: PID of the session server that died; 0 when unknown (reason server_absent_at_start).

server_started_at.description: When that server process started (RFC 3339 with offset); null when unknown.

detected_at.description: When the watchdog saw the server gone (RFC 3339 with offset).

reason.description: panic: the zellij log holds a panic for this server. oom_killed: the kernel OOM killer took it. server_absent_at_start: the watchdog started and found no server for a session it manages (reboot, power loss). unknown: it is gone and no cause was found.

panic.description: The panic the zellij log recorded, when reason is panic; null otherwise.

thread.description: Thread that panicked, e.g. async-std/runtime or the screen thread.

location.description: Source location of the panic, file:line:col.

originating.description: The zellij 'Originating Thread' / caller context line, when the log has one.

log_path.description: The zellij log file the cause was read from; null when none was read.

zellij_version.description: zellij --version of the binary that ran the server, when known.
